name: The Royal Match
about: The council says the crown needs an heir, and two great houses each offer a child to wed. Choose one and the other is shamed; choose neither and both turn. Then the childbed, which spares no one for being royal.
title: The Royal Match

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The small council says aloud what the realm whispers: the crown has no heir of its body, and a throne without one is a prize. Two houses answer at once.

court.text: {first} of {first.house} and {second} of {second.house} stand either side of the hall, each with a portrait. "{firstChild} is of age, Your Grace." "So is {secondChild}, and of better blood."

options.label: Wed {firstChild} of {first.house}
options.result: The banns are read for the King and {firstChild}. {second} leaves the hall before the reading ends.

options.label: Wed {secondChild} of {second.house}
options.result: The banns are read for the King and {secondChild}. {first} smiles too widely, and says nothing.

options.label: The King will choose in his own time
options.hint: both houses wait · neither for long
options.result: The portraits go into a cupboard. Both houses begin looking for other friends.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: {second.house} wears grey to the royal wedding. At the feast {second} raises a cup to the bride's health, and to the health of every child she may never bear.

court.text: {second}: "My house has been passed over in front of the realm, Your Grace. Words won't mend it."

options.label: Make amends: a royal gift and a seat on the council (300 gold)
options.result: {second} takes the council seat, and the gold, and bows exactly as low as the law demands.

options.label: The King's choice needs no amends
options.result: The King offers nothing. {second} rides home, and {second.his} letters go out to every enemy of {first.house}.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: {first.house} sends a wedding gift of a silver cradle, beautifully made, with a crack down the middle of it.

court.text: {first}: "You chose {second.house}, Your Grace. The realm saw it. My house will need to see something else."

options.label: Make amends: a royal gift and a seat on the council (300 gold)
options.result: {first} takes the council seat, and the gold, and says the cradle was a jest.

options.label: The King's choice needs no amends
options.result: The King sends the cracked cradle back. {first} has it mended, and keeps it on {first.his} table.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: The quarrel between {first.house} and {second.house} leaves the hall for the field. Banners go up along the border of their lands, and the royal in-laws send to the King for help.

court.text: {first}: "They burn my villages because you honoured one house over another, Your Grace. Stand with your kin, or stand aside."

options.label: Send the royal host to your in-laws
options.result: Royal knights ride to stand beside the Queen's house.

options.label: Broker a peace between them (200 gold)
options.result: The King's heralds stand between the two hosts until both lords are too cold to keep fighting.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The quarrel between {second.house} and {first.house} leaves the hall for the field. Banners go up along the border of their lands, and the royal in-laws send to the King for help.

court.text: {second}: "They burn my villages because you honoured one house over another, Your Grace. Stand with your kin, or stand aside."

options.label: Send the royal host to your in-laws
options.result: Royal knights ride to stand beside the Queen's house.

options.label: Broker a peace between them (200 gold)
options.result: The King's heralds stand between the two hosts until both lords are too cold to keep fighting.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: Two winters and no royal wedding. {first} and {second}, who agree on nothing, are seen riding together, and the word in the taverns is that the realm will choose its own heir.

court.text: {second}: "The realm is tired of waiting, Your Grace. Choose now, or the lords will choose for you, and not a bride."

options.label: Wed {firstChild} of {first.house}, now
options.result: The King weds {firstChild} within the month, in haste and in rain.

options.label: Wed {secondChild} of {second.house}, now
options.result: The King weds {secondChild} within the month, in haste and in rain.

options.label: The King will not be hurried to the altar
options.hint: both houses −15 · they choose an heir of their own
options.result: The King refuses. {first} and {second} leave together.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: At {first.seat}, {first} and {second} swear on the old stones that a King with no heir is no King at all, and {first} marches on Kingsmere to be the realm's protector.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: {second} stops calling it a quarrel between houses. {second.His} heralds read a new claim: that the crown has made itself one house's creature, and must be unmade.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: {first} stops calling it a quarrel between houses. {first.His} heralds read a new claim: that the crown has made itself one house's creature, and must be unmade.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The Queen is with child. The midwives come from three houses, and none of them trusts the other two. All Kingsmere waits under the windows.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The child is born living, and the Queen does not see the morning. {first}, her {first.father}, demands to know which midwife washed her hands, and which did not.

court.text: {first}, in mourning black: "My blood died in your bed, Your Grace. Give my house the raising of the child, or give me the midwife who killed her."

options.label: Give the Queen's house the raising of the heir
options.result: The heir goes to be raised by the Queen's kin. They swear the child will know its mother's face from the portraits.

options.label: The heir stays at Kingsmere, with the King
options.result: The heir stays at Kingsmere. The Queen's father does not come to the naming.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: The child is born living, and the Queen does not see the morning. {second}, her {second.father}, demands to know which midwife washed her hands, and which did not.

court.text: {second}, in mourning black: "My blood died in your bed, Your Grace. Give my house the raising of the child, or give me the midwife who killed her."

options.label: Give the Queen's house the raising of the heir
options.result: The heir goes to be raised by the Queen's kin. They swear the child will know its mother's face from the portraits.

options.label: The heir stays at Kingsmere, with the King
options.result: The heir stays at Kingsmere. The Queen's father does not come to the naming.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: One of the King's two promised brides is dead, and the other house is accused of it before the body is cold.

beats.speaker: first
beats.text: The bells of Kingsmere ring for a royal heir, loud and healthy. The lords who wanted the throne for themselves come to the naming, and kneel to the cradle.

beats.speaker: second
beats.text: The lords who would have chosen the King's heir for him are broken. He rules on with no Queen and no heir, and the realm learns to stop asking.
